scope: Proposition 7.4 (Marks with an arbitrary toll) of the manuscript “No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation” (preprints/No-bigeodesics-in-planar-first-passage-percolation-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 212 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f97d87dc82bcee0c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With R0 fixed as above, for every positive integer M the common coupling defines marks JM (k) ∈ {0, 1} at all horizontal sites, with the same marginal probability at each site and (73) P(JM (k) = 1) ≥ p/4. A mark selects a bigeodesic pk in Tk,R(M) through k, with upper label ρk ∈ I avoiding all partition endpoints. Its arms lie in Q±(k, H0). Its first R(M) upper-arm edges have total increase at least M over the base environment, and one of its first R0 upper-arm edges has increase at least g. All changes occur in a deterministic bounded neighborhood of k whose radius may depend on M.
